questiontext.text:
Question ID: MLA.ENG1.C.02 U06 L05 Q01

MLA Standard: MLA.ENG1.C.02 Perspective: Weekly planning helps students manage long-term assignments. Which slide note is clearest? \

answer.text: A. Weekly planning breaks long assignments into manageable steps.

feedback.text: Correct. This note is concise and clearly supports the presentation perspective.

answer.text: B. Planning has a lot of stuff that happens.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This wording is vague and does not help the audience understand the point.

answer.text: C. Assignments are things students do.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This is too general and does not support the perspective.

answer.text: D. There are many weeks in a school year.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This fact does not explain how weekly planning helps.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: MLA.ENG1.RS.01 U06 L05 Q02

MLA Standard: MLA.ENG1.RS.01 Which source is most credible for a slide about online source evaluation? \

answer.text: A. An anonymous post with no author or date

feedback.text: Incorrect. Missing source information makes the evidence weak for an academic presentation.

answer.text: B. A meme about copying homework

feedback.text: Incorrect. A meme is not credible evidence for this presentation purpose.

answer.text: C. A friend's unsupported opinion about websites

feedback.text: Incorrect. An unsupported opinion does not provide reliable research evidence.

answer.text: D. A school research guide explaining how to check author, date, and purpose

feedback.text: Correct. This source is relevant, reliable, and connected to source evaluation.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: MLA.ENG1.W.04 U06 L05 Q03

MLA Standard: MLA.ENG1.V.01 Weak slide note: Feedback can help with lots of writing stuff before things get turned in. Which revision is clearest? \

answer.text: A. Feedback and writing things are pretty helpful.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This remains vague and informal. Review the lesson explanation to confirm why this choice fits or does not fit.

answer.text: B. Writing stuff changes sometimes.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This does not explain how feedback helps.

answer.text: C. Feedback helps writers clarify ideas before final submission.

feedback.text: Correct. This revision is concise and clearly explains the idea.

answer.text: D. Feedback happens when people say things.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This is too broad and does not support the presentation perspective.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: MLA.ENG1.V.01 U06 L05 Q04

MLA Standard: MLA.ENG1.W.04 Which phrase uses academic vocabulary best on a slide about evidence? \

answer.text: A. source stuff

feedback.text: Incorrect. This phrase is vague and informal.

answer.text: B. credible evidence from reliable sources

feedback.text: Correct. This phrase is precise and appropriate for a digital presentation.

answer.text: C. things from somewhere

feedback.text: Incorrect. This wording does not identify evidence precisely.

answer.text: D. facts and stuff

feedback.text: Incorrect. This is informal and too broad. Review the lesson explanation to confirm why this choice fits or does not fit.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: MLA.ENG1.C.02 U06 L05 Q05

MLA Standard: MLA.ENG1.C.02 A slide contains a full paragraph copied from a source. What is the best revision? \

answer.text: A. Replace the paragraph with a concise evidence note and explain the details orally.

feedback.text: Correct. This keeps the slide readable while preserving the evidence.

answer.text: B. Add a second paragraph so the slide looks complete.

feedback.text: Incorrect. More text would overload the audience.

answer.text: C. Remove all source information from the presentation.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Evidence is needed, but it should be presented clearly.

answer.text: D. Shrink the font until all the text fits.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Smaller text does not improve clarity or audience awareness.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: MLA.ENG1.RS.01 U06 L05 Q06

MLA Standard: MLA.ENG1.RS.01 Which evidence best supports a presentation about source credibility? \

answer.text: A. A random picture of a computer

feedback.text: Incorrect. A picture alone does not provide evidence about credibility.

answer.text: B. A rumor that websites are usually fine

feedback.text: Incorrect. A rumor is not reliable evidence. Review the lesson explanation to confirm why this choice fits or does not fit.

answer.text: C. A source-checking checklist from the school media center

feedback.text: Correct. Review the lesson explanation to confirm why this choice fits or does not fit.

answer.text: D. A list of unrelated website colors

feedback.text: Incorrect. Website colors do not prove source credibility.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: MLA.ENG1.C.02 U06 L05 Q07

MLA Standard: MLA.ENG1.V.01 Which slide is most audience-aware for ninth-grade students beginning research? \

answer.text: A. "Epistemological source triangulation protocols"

feedback.text: Incorrect. This wording is too advanced and may confuse the intended audience.

answer.text: B. "Sources are sources, so just use them."

feedback.text: Incorrect. This is inaccurate and not audience-aware.

answer.text: C. "Research is impossible to understand."

feedback.text: Incorrect. This discourages the audience and does not teach a clear strategy.

answer.text: D. "Check who wrote the source, when it was published, and why it was created."

feedback.text: Correct. This wording is clear and useful for ninth-grade students.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: MLA.ENG1.W.04 U06 L05 Q08

MLA Standard: MLA.ENG1.W.04 Which revision improves slide cohesion? \

answer.text: A. Use a slide title that connects the evidence to the presentation perspective.

feedback.text: Correct. Review the lesson explanation to confirm why this choice fits or does not fit.

answer.text: B. Put unrelated evidence on the same slide.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Unrelated evidence weakens cohesion.

answer.text: C. Add random facts from several topics.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Random facts weaken cohesion. Review the lesson explanation to confirm why this choice fits or does not fit.

answer.text: D. Remove the connection between evidence and claim.

feedback.text: Incorrect. The audience needs that connection.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: MLA.ENG1.V.01 U06 L05 Q09

MLA Standard: MLA.ENG1.C.02 Which word best completes the slide note? "Use _____ evidence to support digital presentation claims." \

answer.text: A. decorative

feedback.text: Incorrect. Decoration is not the same as evidence.

answer.text: B. credible

feedback.text: Correct. Credible evidence is trustworthy and appropriate for support.

answer.text: C. random

feedback.text: Incorrect. Random evidence would not provide trustworthy support.

answer.text: D. confusing

feedback.text: Incorrect. Confusing evidence would weaken audience understanding.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: MLA.ENG1.C.02 U06 L05 Q10

MLA Standard: MLA.ENG1.RS.01 Which slide note is too vague? \

answer.text: A. Source checks help students avoid outdated information.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This is clear and specific. Review the lesson explanation to confirm why this choice fits or does not fit.

answer.text: B. Written due dates help students track long-term assignments.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This is specific and understandable.

answer.text: C. Stuff helps people do things better.

feedback.text: Correct. This note is too vague to support a digital presentation.

answer.text: D. Feedback can reveal unclear evidence before final submission.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This clearly supports a presentation point.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: MLA.ENG1.RS.01 U06 L05 Q11

MLA Standard: MLA.ENG1.V.01 A student finds evidence but cannot identify the author, date, or source. What should the student do? \

answer.text: A. Put it on a slide without explanation.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Unverified evidence weakens credibility.

answer.text: B. Use it because all online information is reliable.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Online information must be evaluated.

answer.text: C. Use it only if it is colorful.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Visual appeal does not prove reliability.

answer.text: D. Avoid using it unless the source can be verified.

feedback.text: Correct. Evidence should be reliable and traceable before it supports a presentation.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: MLA.ENG1.W.04 U06 L05 Q12

MLA Standard: MLA.ENG1.W.04 Which slide revision improves clarity? \

answer.text: A. Replace specific wording with unclear abbreviations.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Unclear abbreviations can confuse the audience.

answer.text: B. Change "clear evidence" to "stuff."

feedback.text: Incorrect. This makes the wording less precise.

answer.text: C. Change "evaluation of source reliability" to "checking whether a source can be trusted."

feedback.text: Correct. Review the lesson explanation to confirm why this choice fits or does not fit.

answer.text: D. Add three unrelated examples to the same slide.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This would make the slide less clear.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: MLA.ENG1.C.02 U06 L05 Q13

MLA Standard: MLA.ENG1.C.02 Which choice best explains how evidence should function on a slide? \

answer.text: A. It should decorate the slide even if it does not support the claim.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Evidence is not decoration. Review the lesson explanation to confirm why this choice fits or does not fit.

answer.text: B. It should replace the speaker's entire explanation.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Slides should support, not replace, speaking.

answer.text: C. It should be unrelated so the audience is surprised.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Unrelated evidence breaks coherence.

answer.text: D. It should support the perspective and give the speaker something meaningful to explain.

feedback.text: Correct. Review the lesson explanation to confirm why this choice fits or does not fit.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: MLA.ENG1.V.01 U06 L05 Q14

MLA Standard: MLA.ENG1.RS.01 Which revision uses stronger academic vocabulary? \

answer.text: A. "reliable evidence" instead of "good source stuff"

feedback.text: Correct. Review the lesson explanation to confirm why this choice fits or does not fit.

answer.text: B. "good source stuff" instead of "reliable evidence"

feedback.text: Incorrect. This revision weakens precision. Review the lesson explanation to confirm why this choice fits or does not fit.

answer.text: C. "things that seem okay" instead of "credible sources"

feedback.text: Incorrect. This is vague and informal. Review the lesson explanation to confirm why this choice fits or does not fit.

answer.text: D. "random website facts" instead of "research findings"

feedback.text: Incorrect. This weakens the academic tone. Review the lesson explanation to confirm why this choice fits or does not fit.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: MLA.ENG1.W.04 U06 L05 Q15

MLA Standard: MLA.ENG1.V.01 Weak slide title: "A Lot of Things About Feedback." Which revision is best? \

answer.text: A. Feedback and stuff

feedback.text: Incorrect. This is still vague and informal. Review the lesson explanation to confirm why this choice fits or does not fit.

answer.text: B. Why Feedback Improves Final Drafts

feedback.text: Correct. Review the lesson explanation to confirm why this choice fits or does not fit.

answer.text: C. Many things happen

feedback.text: Incorrect. This does not identify the slide's focus.

answer.text: D. Words on a slide

feedback.text: Incorrect. This is not a meaningful title. Review the lesson explanation to confirm why this choice fits or does not fit.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: MLA.ENG1.C.02 U06 L05 Q16

MLA Standard: MLA.ENG1.W.04 Which slide note best supports a presentation for school leaders? \

answer.text: A. Some papers are long.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This does not support a clear presentation perspective.

answer.text: B. Student survey results show that written reminders reduce missed due dates.

feedback.text: Correct. This evidence is specific, credible, and appropriate for school leaders.

answer.text: C. Due dates are annoying to lots of people.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This is informal and unsupported. Review the lesson explanation to confirm why this choice fits or does not fit.

answer.text: D. Everybody knows reminders are good.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This assumes support instead of providing evidence.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: MLA.ENG1.RS.01 U06 L05 Q17

MLA Standard: MLA.ENG1.C.02 Which question helps evaluate source reliability? \

answer.text: A. Who created the source and why was it created?

feedback.text: Correct. Review the lesson explanation to confirm why this choice fits or does not fit.

answer.text: B. Does the source have many colors?

feedback.text: Incorrect. Color does not determine credibility.

answer.text: C. Is the source title written in a large font?

feedback.text: Incorrect. Font size does not prove reliability.

answer.text: D. Can the source be copied quickly?

feedback.text: Incorrect. Ease of copying is not a reliability measure.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: MLA.ENG1.W.04 U06 L05 Q18

MLA Standard: MLA.ENG1.RS.01 Which feedback would best help revise a slide? \

answer.text: A. "Add more random colors."

feedback.text: Incorrect. Color alone does not improve evidence or clarity.

answer.text: B. "Use every fact you found."

feedback.text: Incorrect. Too many facts can overload a slide.

answer.text: C. "Remove the main perspective."

feedback.text: Incorrect. The perspective is needed for coherence.

answer.text: D. "Make the evidence connection clearer for the audience."

feedback.text: Correct. Review the lesson explanation to confirm why this choice fits or does not fit.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: MLA.ENG1.C.02 U06 L05 Q19

MLA Standard: MLA.ENG1.V.01 Which slide text is most concise and clear? \

answer.text: A. The thing that we are trying to say is that sources should be looked at carefully before using them.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This is wordy for a slide. Review the lesson explanation to confirm why this choice fits or does not fit.

answer.text: B. Sources and evidence and things and looking.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This is unclear and incomplete. Review the lesson explanation to confirm why this choice fits or does not fit.

answer.text: C. Check sources before using evidence.

feedback.text: Correct. Review the lesson explanation to confirm why this choice fits or does not fit.

answer.text: D. Research maybe needs stuff checked sometimes.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This is vague and uncertain. Review the lesson explanation to confirm why this choice fits or does not fit.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: MLA.ENG1.V.01 U06 L05 Q20

MLA Standard: MLA.ENG1.W.04 Which academic word best replaces "good enough to trust"? \

answer.text: A. credible

feedback.text: Correct. Review the lesson explanation to confirm why this choice fits or does not fit.

answer.text: B. crowded

feedback.text: Incorrect. Crowded describes too much content, not reliability.

answer.text: C. colorful

feedback.text: Incorrect. Colorful does not mean trustworthy.

answer.text: D. random

feedback.text: Incorrect. Random information is not necessarily trustworthy.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: MLA.ENG1.C.02 U06 L05 Q21

MLA Standard: MLA.ENG1.C.02 A slide note says, "Student survey: written reminders reduce missed deadlines." What should the speaker do orally? \

answer.text: A. Read the note and immediately stop speaking.

feedback.text: Incorrect. The audience needs explanation. Review the lesson explanation to confirm why this choice fits or does not fit.

answer.text: B. Ignore the slide and discuss an unrelated topic.

feedback.text: Incorrect. The oral explanation should connect to the slide.

answer.text: C. Add a full paragraph to the slide while speaking.

feedback.text: Incorrect. The slide should stay concise. Review the lesson explanation to confirm why this choice fits or does not fit.

answer.text: D. Explain how the survey supports the presentation's perspective.

feedback.text: Correct. The speaker should connect the concise slide note to the larger idea.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: MLA.ENG1.W.04 U06 L05 Q22

MLA Standard: MLA.ENG1.RS.01 Which revision best improves audience awareness? \

answer.text: A. Replace clear student-friendly wording with technical jargon.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Jargon can confuse the audience. Review the lesson explanation to confirm why this choice fits or does not fit.

answer.text: B. Choose examples and vocabulary the intended audience can understand.

feedback.text: Correct. Review the lesson explanation to confirm why this choice fits or does not fit.

answer.text: C. Remove all explanations from the slides and speech.

feedback.text: Incorrect. The audience still needs support. Review the lesson explanation to confirm why this choice fits or does not fit.

answer.text: D. Add unrelated facts to impress the audience.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Unrelated facts weaken clarity. Review the lesson explanation to confirm why this choice fits or does not fit.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: MLA.ENG1.RS.01 U06 L05 Q23

MLA Standard: MLA.ENG1.V.01 Which evidence should be avoided? \

answer.text: A. A dated school survey with clear results

feedback.text: Incorrect. This is likely usable evidence. Review the lesson explanation to confirm why this choice fits or does not fit.

answer.text: B. A teacher observation connected to the topic

feedback.text: Incorrect. This can be relevant evidence. Review the lesson explanation to confirm why this choice fits or does not fit.

answer.text: C. An online post with no author, source, or support

feedback.text: Correct. Review the lesson explanation to confirm why this choice fits or does not fit.

answer.text: D. A research guide from the media center

feedback.text: Incorrect. This is a credible source for research guidance.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: MLA.ENG1.C.02 U06 L05 Q24

MLA Standard: MLA.ENG1.W.04 Which slide plan best balances evidence and clarity? \

answer.text: A. Several unrelated facts in small font

feedback.text: Incorrect. This weakens clarity and coherence.

answer.text: B. One concise evidence note plus oral explanation

feedback.text: Correct. Review the lesson explanation to confirm why this choice fits or does not fit.

answer.text: C. Five copied paragraphs on one slide

feedback.text: Incorrect. This would overload the audience. Review the lesson explanation to confirm why this choice fits or does not fit.

answer.text: D. No evidence and only a decorative image

feedback.text: Incorrect. The presentation still needs support.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: MLA.ENG1.W.04 U06 L05 Q25

MLA Standard: MLA.ENG1.C.02 A slide is accurate but hard to understand. What should the student do? \

answer.text: A. Leave it unchanged because accuracy is the only concern.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Digital presentations also need clarity and audience awareness.

answer.text: B. Remove the evidence and use decoration instead.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Evidence should remain if it supports the perspective.

answer.text: C. Add more complex words to make it sound harder.

feedback.text: Incorrect. More complex wording may reduce audience understanding.

answer.text: D. Revise the wording so the accurate idea is easier for the audience to follow.

feedback.text: Correct. Revision should preserve accuracy while improving clarity.
